summary.headline: Cello World Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.8% YoY to INR633.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.3% from 24% on gas and polymer cost inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR633.2 crore, up 7.8% YoY and 20.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR135 crore (21.3% margin) and PAT of INR81.9 crore (12.9%). Management attributed the soft Consumerware quarter to festive demand shifting into Q3 and to the steelware ramp-up, and said H1 and Q2 are not strictly comparable with last year. Cost pressure from the West Asia conflict, polymer, fuel and gas prices compressed margins, with glassware only breaking even. Management guided to about 10% revenue growth for FY27 and declined to give margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 49.5% in Q2 FY26; lower QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Consumerware 64.8%, Writing Instruments 21.5%, Moulded Furniture and Allied 13.7%
General trade 70.3%, online 15.7%, export 8.1%, modern trade 5.9%
financial_highlights.change: online profitability in line with general trade

segments.name: Consumerware
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue flat at INR417.2 crore as festive demand shifted to Q3 and steelware ramp-up slowed growth. Steelware de-grew; glassware grew and opalware grew marginally.

segments.name: Writing Instruments
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 69.5% YoY led by the Cello brand; Cello Pens margins are well below Unomax, which management says is less than one-third of Unomax's profit margin level.

segments.name: Moulded Furniture and Allied Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.8 crore, down 6.5% YoY; management is prioritising revenue and profitability over growth as polymer prices rose 30-40% and about 60% of cost is raw material.

guidance_outlook: Consumerware and overall revenue growth of about 10% YoY by end of FY27; the Writing Instruments acquisition supports growth.
FY28 and FY29 growth of 17-18% was floated as a hope and a working target, not committed.
Management refused to give FY27 margin guidance, but said margins will be significantly higher from here and much better next year.
Steel bottle product range to be widened to about 50-55 SKUs by December, with the impact on sales seen in the following quarter.
Glassware furnace restart by December after a 1.5-month maintenance upgrade; utilisation to rise thereafter.
Glassware and opalware combined revenue of close to INR550 crore targeted for FY27, which management said is about 25-27% of total revenue.
capex_capacity: Steelware capacity about 5 million pieces, currently running at about 2 million; two additional lines to be installed and commissioned next quarter.
Glassware utilisation about 60%; temporary halt for machinery upgrade to improve product mix, with inventory being drawn down, and restart expected by December.

Opalware utilisation about 80%, with a marginal YoY increase; target about 85% by year-end and full capacity next year. Brownfield expansion decision in early calendar 2027 (12-14 month build near the glass plant).
Capex: most major capex is done; going forward only maintenance capex.
Working capital: inventory elevated due to glassware; receivables targeted to fall by 5-7 days; overall cycle target of 10-15 days.
demand_pricing: Steelware demand is above supply; ramp-up is constrained by technical difficulty and efficiency, with heating issues now being resolved.

Glassware price hike of about 10% taken in the quarter, plus product mix change; Chinese low-price imports and freight costs remain a pressure. A minimum import price (MIP) application is under government consideration.
Opalware price hike of about 10% taken with volumes held.
No further price hike in Q2 or planned for steelware; the last price increase was taken in Q1.
Glassware gas prices (about 30% of cost) doubled from INR53-54 per unit; higher realisations offset this, leaving glassware EBITDA-neutral.
Channel inventory is low after festive season; October described as a good month. Moulded Furniture is affected by polymer prices.

qa_highlights.question: Opalware and glassware utilisation and YoY growth, and when glassware reaches optimum utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Opalware about 80% utilisation with marginal growth, aiming for about 85% by year-end. Glassware at 60%, with revenue rising QoQ; utilisation to rise as older inventory is cleared and the furnace restarts.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook given falling crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polymer prices remain high and the impact of lower crude would flow through in about 1.5 months, so gross margin expansion is expected after that. Lower gas prices would also help glassware.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue growth targets for FY27 and the next few years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% growth by end-FY27, with Consumerware expected to grow. FY28 and FY29 growth of 17-18% was described as a hope that depends on momentum and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel bottle in-house production replace lost import-linked sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Product range to reach about 50-55 SKUs by December, with the sales impact seen in the following quarter. The company expects to be self-sufficient on supply then.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Moulded Furniture declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer prices rose 30-40%, and raw material is about 60% of cost, so volumes fell. Management expects revenue to recover when the cycle turns down.

qa_highlights.question: Is glassware EBITDA-neutral and what restart costs are involved?
qa_highlights.answer: Glassware broke even in Q2. Restart costs were already provided for and are limited.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing three drags (steelware efficiency, gas prices and Cello Pens margins), and said margins can be significantly higher from here.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash and return on equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Large cash balance; management is looking for an acquisition or a new vertical, preferably synergistic, and expects better ROE once the glass and steel issues settle.

risks_watch: Gas and polymer prices: management said margin recovery depends on crude and gas declining, and its own margin outlook is conditional on these.
Steelware ramp-up: utilisation about 2 million of 5 million pieces, with efficiency still short of target and two new lines due next quarter.
Chinese glassware imports and freight costs, plus pending MIP outcome.
Moulded Furniture volume decline, given the segment is crowded and polymer-driven.
Working capital: inventory and receivables still high; receivable reduction and inventory normalisation to be tracked next quarter.
Festive timing: Q3 is expected to carry demand shifted from Q2, which makes Q2 and H1 comparisons difficult.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and future margin recovery, but cautious on near-term margins; management openly declined to give FY27 margin guidance and framed the year as one of transition for steelware, glassware and Cello Pens.
key_quotes: Overall, price efficiencies have come in, product mix is becoming a lot better, but overall, due to the higher gas prices, margins are impacted.
It has de-grown because of supply, not demand. I think, when we are solving for supply, demand is already out there.
I would refrain from giving you a margin guidance. It will definitely be better because this year we have been hit by three things.
Capex, not much. We have done most of the capex. It will just be maintenance capex going forward.

adds.what: Steelware two additional lines (steelware capacity ~5 million pieces, running ~2 million)
Opalware brownfield expansion near glass plant (12-14 month build; decision early calendar 2027)

growth.why: Management reiterated about 10% revenue growth for FY27 (Consumerware plus Writing Instruments, with the acquisition supporting growth) and targets glassware plus opalware near INR550 crore; backing is partial, with steelware lines due next quarter, glassware furnace restart by December, and a price hike, but no committed margin guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margins will be significantly higher from here as crude and gas costs fall and glassware price hikes flow through, with gross margin expansion expected about 1.5 months after the crude decline; EBITDA margin was 21.3% in Q2 vs 24% last year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (steelware lines); Q4 FY27 (glassware restart)
rows.why: Steelware runs ~2 million of ~5 million pieces with two new lines due next quarter; glassware furnace restarts by December after a 1.5-month upgrade, but the opalware brownfield is only a decision in early calendar 2027 with a 12-14 month build, so it is outside the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Glassware at 60% utilisation with furnace restart by December and steelware at 2 million of 5 million pieces give room to grow, but Moulded Furniture volumes fell 6.5% YoY and Q2 consumerware was flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says most major capex is done and only maintenance capex follows; the one new project (opalware brownfield) is already in planning with a decision due early calendar 2027, so no fresh capex announcement is signalled in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue growth is only held at about 10% for FY27 and H1 growth was just 3.9%, so the company is not positioned to raise guidance in the window.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give FY27 margin guidance, EBITDA margin fell to 21.3% from 24%, and gas and polymer costs remain high; ~10% FY27 revenue growth is held but depends on Q3 festive catch-up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (steel bottle SKUs by December)
rows.why: Steel bottle range to widen to about 50-55 SKUs by December, with sales impact in the following quarter, a move that replaces import-linked sales.

rows.label: Steelware demand above supply
rows.why: Steelware demand is above supply and ramp-up depends on heating and efficiency fixes; two new lines are due next quarter against 2 million of 5 million pieces run today.

rows.label: Minimum import price (MIP) on Chinese glassware
rows.why: MIP application is under government consideration against Chinese low-price imports, which management cites as a pressure on glassware.

rows.label: Receivable days cut 5-7 days
rows.why: Management targets receivables down 5-7 days and an overall cash cycle of 10-15 days, with inventory elevated by glassware.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand and future margin recovery but cautious on near-term margins and declined to guide FY27 margins; analysts pushed on gas, polymer and crude pass-through, steelware efficiency and the FY28-29 growth targets.
